newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sharholders' group opposes choice on accounting.
newsitem.headline: Sharholders' group opposes choice on accounting.

text.p: The Australian Shareholders' Association (ASA) said on Monday a move to allow companies to choose either equity accounting or the cost method of accounting would give official sanction to corporate window dressing.
Some companies would adopt equity accounting to make their results look better, the association said.
"Others will continue to report under the existing accounting standard because their result would look if they used equity accounting," it said in a statement.

The Australian Securities Commission earlier this month said it would issue orders clearing the way for companies to use equity accounting in their accounts for the financial year ending June 30, 1997.

Equity accounting -- which is used in the United States and Britain -- requires companies to bring a proportionate share of the after-tax profits of an associated company into their profit and loss statement.
An associate is defined as a financial entity in which the investing company can exercise significant influence, but does not have control.
Under current accounting standards an investment in an associated company is carried in the books at cost and does not affect the profit and loss statement.
The ASA said it did not oppose equity accounting, but believed one standard should apply to all companies.
The decision to permit equity accounting would make company performance comparisons even more difficult than at present, as shareholders would be "comparing apples and pears".
"This gives official sanction to corporate window dressing," it said.
